boundary_cases.description: A local patch is attempted, but testing reveals wider adhesion problems before full restoration.
boundary_cases.reason: Classify by maximum repair scope needed before first qualifying restoration, not the initial repair plan.

boundary_cases.description: Officials declare success after a quick refill, but peeling resumes before testing or credible verification establishes normal operation.
boundary_cases.reason: A premature announcement is not qualifying completion; the reversal forces rework before the first qualifying restoration.

boundary_cases.description: A fully repaired and normally operating pool is credibly verified before the deadline, then suffers a separate later failure.
boundary_cases.reason: If the first qualifying restoration required local work and no external interruption, this remains the local branch; the before-deadline event already occurred. A different original contract persistence requirement would require reconciliation.

boundary_cases.description: A court-driven pause interrupts a physically small repair.
boundary_cases.reason: External interruption takes precedence in the hierarchical partition.

payload.partition_review: The hierarchy avoids double counting external delay with work scope. Completion is defined by actual restored operation, not a political declaration.
